ig_carousel_topic.topic: What 'units' actually mean (and why win % alone is a lie)
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text:
Win rate doesn't tell you if you're making money.
Units do.
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors track wins and losses.
"I'm 6-4 this week!" Sounds great.
But if the 4 losses were -1.5u each and the 6 wins were +0.6u each, you're down money.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
A unit is a fixed percentage of your bankroll. Usually 1-2%.
Tracking units shows profit or loss in real terms, not just a scoreboard.
54% win rate means nothing without knowing average odds and stake size.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Example: 10 bets at 1u each.
6 wins at -110 odds = +5.45u
4 losses at -110 odds = -4.00u
Net: +1.45u. Positive.
Now flip it: 6 wins at -200, 4 losses at +150.
Net: -0.0u or worse. Same win rate. Different result.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
The honest target is 53-58% at standard -110 lines.
Anyone claiming 70%+ is either cherry-picking or lying.
Track units. That's the only number that matters at the end of the month.
